solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do not be tempted by ugly sister

indicators.note: something ugly has been knocked out of shape, so the letters of sister are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice from a fairy tale: don't fall for the charms of the Ugly Sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ugly sister' reads as Cinderella's stepsister, but 'ugly' is the anagram signal on SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand a temptation is to refuse to give in, so the verb phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Hunting vermin is pointless with a northern playwright

indicators.note: a compass point, N, is dropped, leaving the word without a point

parts.note: ratting is the hunting of rats
a gives A and N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A rat-catching chore described as futile, oddly paired with a playwright from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points N, S, E and W are 'points' in crosswords, so 'pointless' removes one of them, here the N of RATTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, author of The Winslow Boy and The Browning Version.

clue.text: Most frugal cuts set in stone

indicators.note: the word for cuts is placed inside the letters for stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
to pare is to cut or trim, so cuts gives pares

explanation.surface: A sculptor's economy: the fewest possible cuts carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means meagre or economical, so its superlative describes the most sparing.

clue.text: Quiet individual excelled

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an individual is a single one

explanation.surface: A shy, quiet person turned out to be outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine at something is to be outstanding, so the past tense matches excelled.

clue.text: Religious leaders maybe bless ushers on a regular basis

indicators.note: taking every other letter at regular intervals, starting from the second letter of maybe

explanation.surface: Church dignitaries might bless the ushers routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' looks like a link to the definition, but it is part of the letter run: the even letters of MAYBE BLESS USHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbesses head communities of nuns, so they are female religious superiors.

clue.text: Burt Lancaster, initially, when prime minister could have met three sisters here

definitions.text: could have met three sisters here

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the two names is taken

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Ted Heath was the British Conservative prime minister of 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A film star's initials and a former prime minister gather where three sisters might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was UK prime minister from 1970 to 1974. The three sisters are Macbeth's weird sisters, the witches he meets on a blasted heath, not Chekhov's.
explanation.definitionFit: In Macbeth the witches meet Macbeth on a desolate moor, the place this definition describes.

clue.text: Ancient Greeks record material with centre part moved to the end

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.text: centre part moved to the end
indicators.note: the middle letter of the fabric word is shifted to its final position

parts.note: hessian is a coarse jute fabric

explanation.surface: A music record and some cloth, rearranged into a description of old Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre part moved to the end' takes the middle S of HESSIAN to the end, giving HESIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Ephesus, an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, to whom Paul wrote an epistle.

clue.text: American muscle in a way dodgy

indicators.note: the American and muscle letters are placed inside the street letters

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
US stands for United States, so American
a pec is a pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: An American bodybuilder seen in a street looking rather shady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is questionable or of doubtful honesty, the same sense as dodgy.

clue.text: Some disheartened by identical plant

indicators.note: removing the heart, the middle letters, leaves only the outer letters of the word

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: Some people are dismayed by a plant just like another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a herbaceous plant grown for its oil-rich seeds.

clue.text: Volunteers to keep key drug in crockery

indicators.note: the volunteer letters hold the key inside them

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
E is a musical key
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Army volunteers hiding a key and some drugs in the crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the UK's part-time volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapot is a piece of crockery, so the definition names a class it belongs to.

clue.text: Sovereign takes pains with Iceland's fate

parts.note: a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L for libra
aches are pains
IS is the international vehicle code for Iceland

explanation.surface: A monarch goes to great trouble over Iceland's destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold coin worth one pound; L stands for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Lachesis is one of the three Fates, the one who measures the thread of life.

clue.text: Distracted, I spoil a march, not seeing the bigger picture

indicators.note: distracted means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone admits a lapse of attention ruined a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochialism is narrowness of outlook, a focus on local concerns over wider ones.

clue.text: Graceless supporter one caught in current trap

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the supporter and one are held inside the current and trap letters

parts.note: a net is a trap
a leg supports a table or chair
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: A clumsy fan gets snagged in a current's net.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace or refinement, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Power plant part includes one

indicators.note: the stem letters take in the letter for one

parts.note: a stem is part of a plant
a means one

explanation.surface: A section of a power station contains one unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power plant' reads as a power station; split it, 'Power' is the definition and 'plant part' gives STEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is the force that drives engines, so it stands for power or energy.

clue.text: Taking part of Toad almost his downfall, to be completely honest

parts.note: acting is taking a part in a play

indicators.note: a downfall is a collapse, so the letters are thrown into disorder
almost the whole word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Playing Toad in Wind in the Willows, almost to the point of his ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims HIS to HI; 'downfall' shuffles OF TOAD HI into OODFAITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something sincerely and without deceit is the idiom's sense of honest dealing.

clue.text: Happy couple will yawn off and on being overwhelmed by requirements

indicators.note: the picked letters are swamped by, so placed inside, the requirements word

parts.note: needs are requirements

indicators.note: letters are taken intermittently, every other one starting from the first

explanation.surface: A bored partner keeps yawning, buried under demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' takes W, L, Y, W from WILL YAWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A just-married pair is conventionally called the happy couple at a wedding.

clue.text: Is obliged to hear about society in Shropshire town

indicators.note: the obliged word goes around the society letter

parts.note: someone who owes is under an obligation
to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: Duty-bound to listen to talk of local society in a Shropshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border; Oswestry is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswestry is a market town in Shropshire near the Welsh border, so it is an example.

clue.text: Stormy Weather is his, with special backing from Carol

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are tossed about
the special letters are put in reverse order

explanation.surface: The song Stormy Weather belongs to him, specially sung with a carol.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a traditional English Christmas song, so it is an example of a carol.

clue.text: Support without winning Queen's Teaspoon?

indicators.note: the winning letters are taken out of the support word

parts.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot
to be up is to be ahead or winning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about backing a losing royal teaspoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes UP from STIRRUP to leave STIRR. The question mark marks a definition by example: a teaspoon is one thing that stirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is used to mix tea in the cup, so it serves as a stirring utensil.

clue.text: One sort of fertiliser not round like reptiles

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the round letter is removed from the fertiliser word

parts.note: guano is bird or bat droppings used as fertiliser
O is round in shape
as means like

explanation.surface: A fertiliser that isn't round, compared to reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical lizards, so they are members of the reptile class.

clue.text: Fought being restrained

definitions.meaning: duelled with swords, as in the sport of swordplay
shut in behind a barrier, enclosed

explanation.surface: A battler who has been held back.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both swordplay and being enclosed by a barrier, two separate senses.

clue.text: See about note for one of three sisters

indicators.note: the see letters go around the note

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see
mi is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A cathedral's view of a note left for a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire. The three sisters are the Brontës.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë, author of Wuthering Heights, was one of the three Brontë sisters.

clue.text: Quality cats essentially praise

indicators.note: the essence of the word is its middle letters

parts.note: a tribute is an act of praise

explanation.surface: The basic merit of cats is that they deserve praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or property, so it is a synonym of quality.

clue.text: One of Chekhov's sisters fashionable in Irish academy

indicators.note: the fashionable word sits inside the Irish academy letters

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A Chekhov heroine finds herself in vogue at an Irish college.
explanation.definitionFit: Irina is the youngest of the Prozorov sisters in Chekhov's play Three Sisters.

clue.text: One of three sisters gets my back trouble after clearing out doghouse

indicators.note: the reversed trouble word comes after the doghouse letters

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: the inside of the word is emptied, leaving its outer letters
the trouble word is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone back in the doghouse after a bit of trouble with a sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clearing out' leaves DE from DOGHOUSE, and 'back' turns AIL into LIA. The three sisters are King Lear's daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is the youngest of King Lear's three daughters, alongside Goneril and Regan.

clue.text: End of sentimental film about pub singer

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an inn is a pub
E.T. is the Spielberg film; the setter's 'about' only places it next to the pub

explanation.surface: The finale of a soppy film set around a pub singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'about' is loose: the film does not wrap round the pub but simply follows it, so treat the word as placement rather than containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch prized for its song, so it is a songbird.

clue.text: Gloomy party keeps ships in the Middle East

indicators.note: the party letters hold the ships inside

parts.note: a do is a party
arks are ships, like Noah's
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A sombre party holds ships in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Darksome is a literary word for dark or dismal, so it matches gloomy.

clue.text: Soggy god has reason to leave wife

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war

indicators.note: the wife letter departs from the reason word

parts.note: why means a reason, as in 'the whys and wherefores'

explanation.surface: A sodden deity has grounds to walk out on his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy land is boggy and waterlogged, so the word means soggy.
